gaps.sentence: I'm ___ a course in web design this term.
gaps.explanation: do a course is the British English collocation for studying on a course.

gaps.sentence: The children were told not to ___ so much noise.
gaps.explanation: make a noise / make noise is the fixed collocation.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ a diary since she was twelve.
gaps.explanation: keep a diary is the fixed collocation for writing in one regularly.

gaps.sentence: Can we ___ a phone call before we leave?
gaps.explanation: make a phone call / make a call is the standard collocation.

gaps.sentence: Students should ___ attention when the teacher is speaking.
gaps.explanation: pay attention is the fixed collocation for listening or concentrating carefully.

gaps.sentence: Ordering your food online can ___ you a lot of time.
gaps.explanation: save somebody time means to make it possible for them to use less time.

gaps.sentence: The manager ___ an announcement about the changes yesterday.
gaps.explanation: make an announcement is the fixed collocation for stating something publicly.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.
